emily: Hey everyone  first day here. M1 MacBook Pro but I previously installed some tools under Rosetta. Brew says `brew --prefix` -> /usr/local and which node -> /usr/local/bin/node. asdf shims exist at ~/.asdf/shims but `node --version` is still the system/x86 node. Any recommended way to clean this up without nuking my brew? Also what's the canonical name for dev keys in 1Password (REDWOOD_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_TEST_KEY)?
nico: welcome! short checklist: 1) Prefer the ARM brew at /opt/homebrew on M1/M2. If you want to keep both you can explicitly call arm brew with `/opt/homebrew/bin/brew` but we recommend reinstalling Homebrew for arm to avoid mixing libs. 2) Ensure asdf shims are prepended in ~/.zprofile: `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` and `eval "$(asdf init zsh)"`. 3) If you installed node via another manager (nvm) remove it: `rm -rf ~/.nvm` and remove nvm lines in your rc. 4) run `asdf plugin-add nodejs || true && asdf install nodejs 18.16.0 && asdf global nodejs 18.16.0 && asdf reshim nodejs`.
sylvia: fwiw we name ephemeral personal keys like `redwood-personal-<github>` in 1Password so look for `redwood-personal-emily` or open a ticket in #support. For local quick testing we prefer direnv: add `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` to a local .envrc and `direnv allow`. Never commit keys to dotfiles.
emily: Thanks! Is there a safe way to migrate brew from /usr/local to /opt/homebrew or should I just reinstall? I have a few global casks I use.
nico: safest is reinstall to arm and then `brew bundle dump` before switch to capture Brewfile of installed taps/casks, then reinstall arm brew and `brew bundle` to restore. Steps: ```
# dump
brew bundle dump --file=~/Brewfile
# reinstall arm brew per brew.sh
# then restore
brew bundle --file=~/Brewfile
```
emo: (typo) ^nico
devex-bot: (bot) Hi emily  If you want hands-on help we offer 30m setup pairings with DevEx. Reply "pair" and I'll DM available slots. See handbook: https://handbook.redwood.dev/onboarding/dev-setup. Also note we have a script `scripts/cleanup-brew-rosetta.sh` in dotfiles to help detect mixed brew installs.
emily: ran `brew bundle dump` and reinstalled arm brew, moved asdf init to ~/.zprofile, reinstalled node with asdf and reshimmed  node now shows v18.16.0. One weird residual: native gems failed until I set openssl flags: `export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib"` and `export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include"` before `asdf install ruby 3.2.2`.
sylvia: yup that's expected. For commit signing gpg pinentry on mac use `brew install pinentry-mac` and set `pinentry-program $(brew --prefix)/bin/pinentry-mac` in ~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf and `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` in ~/.zprofile then restart gpg-agent.
emico: (bot) infra-bot: Reminder: cluster/service credentials live in 1Password and Vault for CI. Ask infra in #infra if you need a scoped CI token.
emily: everything green except one last thing: my devcontainer starts but the project dir is owned by root inside container causing permission errors. Quick fix?
nico: run the devcontainer helper or chown host dir: `sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/projectdir` before launching or use our `scripts/devcontainer-up.sh` which sets uid/gid. If you want we can pair.
emily: awesome, will book a pairing slot. thanks all :tada:
